headers.before: In Luoyang the Third Emperor announces that he will lead the next army himself.
headers.label: Luoyang
headers.why: Pyongyang's walls → the Tang court in Luoyang, with no marker; the reader thinks Wu Zetian is in Pyongyang

headers.before: The someone is the Red Fowl. He comes up the Taedong
headers.label: The Taedong
headers.why: Tang court → the fleet coming up the Taedong, months later

headers.before: In the ninth month, Namseng holds the great river with tens of thousands.
headers.label: The Frozen River
headers.why: Taedong siege → a second front on the Amnok, new cast (Namseng, the White Dragon)

headers.before: In the twelfth month, a letter comes down from the north.
headers.label: Surabol
headers.why: Goguryeo → Silla court, new cast (Munmu, Yushin), months later

headers.before: The courier finds Xue Rengui a thousand miles the other way.
headers.label: The Far West
headers.why: river battle → Xue Rengui on the western frontier, a different war and cast

headers.before: Jinju sends word that he is ill.
headers.label: Sick Leave
headers.why: the campaign at Naesaji → Jinju lounging at home in Surabol

headers.before: Naesaji falls without him. Kim Heumsun takes it in a fortnight
headers.label: The Moon Palace
headers.why: home → the fall of the fort → Munmu's judgment at court; the reader needs to know they are in front of the king

headers.before: Kim Punghun is at Chang’an when the news comes
headers.label: Chang’an
headers.why: Silla court → the emperor's guard in Chang'an, new character

headers.before: On the thirteenth day of the eighth month, with the Silla army already on the road
headers.label: The King Leaves
headers.why: four-banner overview → a live scene in Pung's hall at Juryu; the overview voice slides into dialogue with no cut

headers.before: One fortress doesn't hear it.
headers.label: Imjon
headers.why: the Juryu surrender road → a different fortress holding all autumn, months later, Sangji and Sangya turned

headers.before: Yeon Jungto, who raised the two younger boys at his own table
headers.label: The Southern Border
headers.why: deathbed in Pyongyang → the uncle on the southern border, new character

headers.before: The man he sends is caught at the Pyongyang gate within the week.
headers.label: The Pyongyang Gate
headers.why: Namseng on tour in the provinces → his brothers in the capital

headers.before: He rides back to his own capital and finds the gate shut.
headers.label: The Shut Gate
headers.why: provincial camp → the standoff at the wall; the main confrontation of the episode deserves its own scene

headers.before: Goryeo is nothing but swindlers and thieves
headers.label: Chang’an
headers.why: riding west over the Liao → kneeling before the Third Emperor; the reader can't tell when he arrives

headers.before: Before the captives are shown to the living emperor
headers.label: Zhaoling
headers.why: fallen Pyongyang → the Second Emperor's tomb in Tang, months later

headers.before: The seventeen grades stop at one another.
headers.label: The New Rank
headers.why: Zhaoling → Munmu and Yushin in Silla, the tenth month

headers.before: The bear stays. She comes out a woman on the twenty-first morning
headers.label: The Sacred Birch
headers.why: summary myth → the live courtship scene under the tree

headers.before: Their son is Dangun.
headers.label: Asadal
headers.why: the night under the birch → a son, a capital, fifteen hundred years

headers.before: King Ugeo has stopped sleeping in the palace.
headers.label: The King's Wall
headers.why: two-thousand-year jump and siege overview → a live scene on the wall at night with father and son

headers.before: Munmu gives him a title, a district, and a name for the thing
headers.label: Silla's Guest
headers.why: the Taedong murder → the Silla court and Anseung's new town; the move south is never shown

headers.before: Silla sends an apology to Chang’an and hands back the prisoners.
headers.label: The Apology
headers.why: the battlefield → the court writing the apology, then into Chunchu's flashback

headers.before: He shamed the king’s command and the family name with it.
headers.label: Father's House
headers.why: summary of Stone Gate → Yushin speaking in his house; the reader has no room or listener

headers.before: Yushin goes to the king and asks, in so many words, for his son to be put to death.
headers.label: The King's Hall
headers.why: Yushin's house → Munmu's audience hall

headers.before: Wonsul does not go home. He goes into the hill farms
headers.label: The Hill Farms
headers.why: court → the hill farms, years of exile, a new character (the farmer)

headers.before: Seventh month, 673. He is seventy-nine.
headers.label: The Deathbed
headers.why: the steam cavern → Yushin's house in Surabol on his last night; currently both sit under one header

headers.before: Then the steam goes thin enough to see through, and a man stands on the water
headers.label: The Man on the Water
headers.why: the sisters' scene ends; a new visitor (Dangun) takes over the cave and the register changes from comedy to mandate

headers.before: Out at sea off Cheon Fortress, Xue hears it from a courier
headers.label: The Fleet
headers.why: the horse-cut at Maeso → Xue Rengui at sea

headers.before: In Surabol the number arrives a day ahead of the generals.
headers.label: Surabol
headers.why: Xue's fleet → Munmu's court

headers.before: The last of it happens at the mouth of the Geum
headers.label: Final Ford
headers.why: Tang headquarters leaving Pyongyang in the second month → the Geum estuary in the eleventh month

headers.before: No treaty comes after it, and no envoy.
headers.label: Surabol
headers.why: the estuary fight → the messenger reaching Munmu

headers.before: The cave is a crack in the mountain’s side
headers.label: The Cave
headers.why: the snow march → the cave where the story is told

headers.before: They walk on. Thirty years later the boy will raise a kingdom
headers.label: Thirty Winters On
headers.why: cut to black in the cave → a thirty-year leap to the founding of Balhae

bridges.after: He reached the Yalu. Gaesomun had sent Namseng with tens of thousands
bridges.en: Namseng gets home alive. His father is waiting at the gate.
bridges.ko: 남생은 살아서 돌아온다. 아버지가 성문에서 기다린다.
bridges.why: Gesomun's rebuke follows two quotes with no setting; the reader doesn't know Namseng has come back to Pyongyang

bridges.after: The fangtian ji goes east again.
bridges.en: Back to the river, then. Earlier that morning, Yeon nearly died.
bridges.ko: 다시 강으로 돌아가자. 그날 아침, 연개소문은 죽을 뻔했다.
bridges.why: 'Yumla Defied' jumps back into 'the worst hour of the fighting' after the White Tiger is dead and Xue Rengui is in the far west; it reads as a second battle

bridges.after: …And he will want to move again.
bridges.en: So Boksin takes to his bed, and waits for a visitor.
bridges.ko: 그래서 복신은 병을 핑계로 드러눕고, 손님을 기다린다.
bridges.why: Boksin's private lines under 'The Jar' are followed by a one-line textbook summary of the plot; this turns the summary into a scene beat (cut block 14 when applied)

bridges.after: Yeon Jungto, who raised the two younger boys at his own table
bridges.en: Namgun dictated it. You can hear him trying not to cry.
bridges.ko: 남건이 불러 준 글이다. 울음을 참는 게 들린다.
bridges.why: Namgun's two lines float in after the uncle's letter; it's unclear whether he's speaking, writing, or where he is

bridges.after: The Third Emperor invades Goguryeo again.
bridges.en: He tells a Silla envoy, and tells him to repeat it.
bridges.ko: 그는 신라 사신에게 그렇게 말한다. 그대로 전하라면서.
bridges.why: the emperor's long speech has no listener and no room; 'your country's worry' only makes sense if the reader knows it's addressed to Silla

bridges.after: There is no cruelty in him, which is precisely what makes him difficult
bridges.en: Inside the walls, two brothers watch the eldest come home.
bridges.ko: 성벽 안에서 두 아우가 맏형의 귀향을 지켜본다.
bridges.why: Namsan, Namseng and Namgun each say one line with no staging; the reader can't tell who is inside the walls and who is with the Tang

bridges.after: That night Anseung has him killed.
bridges.en: Then he takes four thousand households south, to Silla.
bridges.ko: 그러고는 사천 호를 이끌고 남쪽 신라로 간다.
bridges.why: Anseung murders Mojam on the Taedong and the next line has him titled by Munmu; the flight to Silla is missing

bridges.after: The King comes to the house himself, which kings do not do.
bridges.en: The old man's eyes are already somewhere younger.
bridges.ko: 노인의 눈은 이미 더 젊은 날에 가 있다.
bridges.why: Yushin answers the king 'Princess…' with no cue; without this the reader thinks it's a typo rather than Yushin seeing Sunduk

stories.logline: The empire tries Pyongyang again: Wu Zetian talks Gaozong out of going himself, the Red Fowl sits down before the walls, Namseng loses the frozen Amnok and is cursed by his father, and the starving Tang army begs Silla for rice until old Yushin volunteers to drive it north.
stories.fixes: It has no protagonist; it hops Pyongyang → Luoyang → Taedong → Amnok → Pyongyang → Surabol in 19 blocks, half of them summary. Pick one spine. Best candidate: Namseng, the heir who loses one river and hears 'I gave you one river' (it plants the brothers' war). Cut the textbook line 'The impenetrable walls of Pyongyang are tested once again' and the duplicate Tang quote (blocks 10 and 11 tell the same crossing). Put block 13 (Red Fowl freezing) straight after block 8 so the siege is one beat. The Yushin offer is a strong last beat; it should end on him loading the carts, and the Rice Road payoff (now at the end of Snake River) should move here or be cut there.

stories.logline: Yeon Gesomun counts the White Tiger's thirteen sons into the Snake River one by one, kills the father, outfaces Yumla's two reapers in the middle of the fight, and the empire hands the dead man's title to Xue Rengui; then Yushin's rice reaches the starving Tang.
stories.fixes: The countdown is the best set piece in the range and works on its own. Three things break it: (1) 'Yumla Defied' happens during the fight but is placed after the father dies and after a cut to the far west; move blocks 38–48 to just before block 25 ('Then only the tiger is left') so the reapers come at the worst hour and Gesomun's 'Not today' powers the last kill; (2) the Xue Rengui coda (34–37) should come last, after the river, as the empire's answer; (3) the Rice Road (49–54) belongs to Pyongyang I, where Yushin volunteers; here it dilutes the Gesomun ending. A better last beat is Gesomun's 'I am… none other than… Yeon Gesomun!!' followed by Xue taking the name.

stories.logline: After the Snake River, the island kingdom of Tamla quietly switches from Baekje to Silla and the Tang.
stories.fixes: Six blocks: two lines of summary, two archival quotes and an end card. Nobody wants anything on the page. Either fold it into White River (block 61 already sends a Tamla envoy up the hill at Juryu, which is the dramatic moment of the switch) or give it a scene: Yuri Dora's envoy weighing three banners on a beach, a one-line bargain, the quote. Its end card repeats Rebellion's opening almost word for word ('Baekje is supposed to be finished. Nobody told the fortresses'); keep it in one place only.

stories.logline: A True Bone general, Kim Jinju, calls in sick for the campaign against a Baekje holdout and is seen at a gyuku match; young Munmu beheads him and his household, and his son in Chang'an quietly decides to wait for a ship.
stories.fixes: Clean shape (sin, judgment, seed of revenge) and the Punghun plant pays off in Maeso. It opens on a header and a summary instead of a hook; open on Jinju's line 'Nineteen generals for one hill fort. They don't need a twentieth.' Cut the archival detour (blocks 12–13 on 'two men of the name'); it is a textbook aside that undercuts the execution. Jinheum is a second name the reader never meets again; drop him from the narration.

stories.logline: Flashback: Boksin and the monk Dochim share the restoration until Dochim gets grand, so Boksin murders him at supper; two years later Boksin plots against King Pung, is caught, spits at his accuser and ends up pickled in a jar while Sangji and Sangya watch and think about switching sides.
stories.fixes: Good arc (the kingmaker eaten by his king) and well set up by Rebellion's 'we have to go back'. Problems: block 1 says 'Before Boksin and the king' but block 7 has Pung already crowned, so the frame is wrong; say 'In the first year of the king'. Block 14 ('Boksin plots to kill the king by pretending to be sick, but is caught and executed instead') is a plot summary that spends the twist before block 15 dramatizes it; cut it. Block 15 cites 'the sixth month of 663', which the next block already implies; drop the year. It overlaps King Pungjang's last third (Boksin resenting the king, the move to Pisong); trim one of them.

stories.logline: Four banners meet at one river mouth: King Pung abandons Juryu to feast a Yamato fleet, Liu Rengui anchors a wall of ships and waits for the tide, Takutsu dies on a burning deck, Pung flees north leaving his sword, and his elder brother Yung, on the Tang flagship, names it and lets him go.
stories.fixes: Strong, with dated scene headers and a real emotional spine (Yung vs Pung). The 'Four Banners' scene is a long overview (blocks 4–9) before anyone speaks; cut the Silla roster numbers ('twenty-eight generals… thirty in another copy') and move straight from Boksin's jar to Pung's announcement. Block 2 ('The epic battle: for the first time the West, Samhan, and the East meet…') is a trailer card; cut it. The tail after Juryu (Imjon and the Yushin/Liu alliance) is three summaries; end on the refugees' quote ('The name of Baekje ends today') or on Sangji's 'I built it', not on the alliance aside.

stories.logline: The Eternal General, who has refused death once, waits for the reapers and gets Yumla himself; he dies in his sleep telling his sons not to fight, and the narrator weighs a man who was right about everything and built nothing.
stories.fixes: The Yumla deathbed works and is set up by the Snake River. The middle is muddy: the uncle Jungto and Namgun's two lines (18–20) are unstaged, and Namgun's 'If the old man were alive we would not be in this state' is a line from after the coup that hasn't happened yet. The epitaph (block 25) re-tells the last-words exchange we just watched, and block 26 spoils the next episode ('his eldest was riding west to show the Third Emperor the road in'). Cut 25, cut the spoiler half of 26, and end on 'He had three sons. How long do you think that lasts?'

stories.logline: Namseng, the new Supreme Commander, tours the provinces; whisperers turn his two brothers against him, a spy is caught, the gate of Pyongyang is shut in his face, and he rides west to kneel to the emperor his father fought.
stories.fixes: The arc is clear but it opens with an unstaged imperial edict in Gaozong's mouth (an archival speech; turn it into a two-line scene or a quote). Block 8 ('A messenger comes to the provincial camp…') adds nothing between the spy's capture and the shut gate; cut it. The killing of Namseng's son exists only inside a quote (block 16); that is the emotional turn of the episode and should be a narrated beat. The gate scene (10–14) ends in Namseng's Joseon speech, which is fine as a plant. The uncle Jungto coda splits the ending; end on Namseng's 'ten thousand years' and the end card.

stories.logline: Three Tang 'beasts' close on Pyongyang with Namseng as guide; Namgun trusts the one man he thinks can't be bought, a monk, who opens the gate; Namgun botches his suicide, the king bows at Zhaoling, and in Silla Munmu invents a rank for Yushin.
stories.fixes: Shinsung's betrayal is the real story and is good. The opening is a jumble of one-line voices (Xue, Namsan, Namseng, Namgun) with no setting, and Namgun's 'Goguryeo… never dies….!' appears twice (blocks 8 and 21); cut the first. Block 16 re-states the gate opening in textbook form right after block 15; cut it. The Yushin promotion is a separate story; it can stay as a coda, but the end card ('The final war begins…!') leads into Mount Gain, which goes back three years. See Mount Gain: this episode should instead end on the Dangun lead-in ('to a bear in a cave…!').

stories.logline: The empire makes Munmu swear brotherhood with Buyeo Yung, the Baekje prince he once spat on, over a white horse, and the only white horse in camp is Yushin's old Hanseul; Yushin walks him up the hill himself.
stories.fixes: A complete, moving story: want (keep the land), obstacle (the oath), cost (the horse), last line ('Find me a war instead'). Its problem is placement: it is 665, but it is read after Pyongyang II (668), where Yushin has already been made Supreme General, so the reader jumps back three years with no warning. Move it to sit right after White River (or between White River and Yeon Gesomun†), give it a new end card teasing Gesomun's deathbed, and give Pyongyang II the bear-in-a-cave lead-in. If it must stay, its first line needs to say it is going back ('Three years before the city fell…'). Also: blocks 1 and 8 give two different time markers ('Two springs after the river', 'The next summer'); keep one.

stories.logline: Myth: heaven's son Hwanung comes down to Mount Taebaek, a bear outlasts a tiger to become a woman and corners him under the birch, their son Dangun founds Joseon; two thousand years later the Han besiege Wanggeom and the city falls because someone inside lifts the bar.
stories.fixes: The jump into it is well set up by Mount Gain's last line. Internally, block 7 ('The long way begins… with a bear') is followed by block 8 ('From there he hands out civilisation') whose 'he' is Hwanung; swap 7 and 8 so the bear line leads into the bear. The two halves (a romance, a siege) are separate stories glued by one header; the siege half is the one the book needs (it plants 'a door opened from the inside' and the six villages of Surabol). Either split the Fall of Joseon into its own short episode or open the episode on the siege and tell the bear as Ugeo's bedtime memory.

stories.logline: After Pyongyang falls, Geom Mojam raises the old flag and crowns a royal cousin, Anseung; they quarrel over whether to fight, Anseung has him killed and takes the survivors south, and Munmu makes him King of Goguryeo inside Silla to annoy the emperor.
stories.fixes: The murder and Munmu's 'Give him a seal. A big one' are good beats, but two back-to-back quotes (3–4) state the setup twice before anyone speaks; keep one. The flight to Silla is missing (see bridge). Opening line repeats Dangun's end card ('Nearly eight hundred years after Wanggeom, the empire… does the same thing again'); open on the quarrel instead. The episode needs one more beat of Anseung himself: a guest-room king with a borrowed seal is a character, and right now he is only a decision.

stories.logline: Xue Rengui tries to win the war by post; Munmu stays up all night dictating a reply that lists every debt Tang owes Silla, the two men trade shorter and ruder notes, and Munmu answers the last one by capturing seventy rice ships.
stories.fixes: Works well and pays off Snake River, Mount Gain and Rebellion. Two clean-ups: block 29 opens 'He comes.' but it is Silla that strikes, not Xue who arrives; change to 'He does not come. His rice does.' Daeto's second letter (block 22) is a good plant that fires in Kim Yushin†; keep it. The episode could end on 'Late. As usual.' and drop the extra card line about chasing.

stories.logline: Silla and the Goguryeo remnants beat the Tang, chase them, and are routed at Seokmun; Silla sends a grovelling apology and starts building, following a plan Chunchu laid out years ago.
stories.fixes: No one on the page wants anything; it's a battle summary, two quotes, a formation box and a flashback. The human story of Stone Gate is Wonsul, who is in the next episode. Merge the two: open on Wonsul in the chase, Danneung grabbing his bridle at the gate, and use Chunchu's flashback as Munmu's reason for the apology. If kept separate, open with a hook instead of 'The Tang take Hansi and Mapeup and come south.'

stories.logline: Yushin's son survives a rout he was told to die in; his father disowns him and asks the king to execute him, the king refuses, and Wonsul goes to work another man's fields under no name.
stories.fixes: A complete little tragedy, but it starts in summary ('is told to die there and does not'), and the 'there' depends on the previous episode. Open on a live beat: Danneung's hand on the bridle, or the closed gate. Block 4 is a narrator lecture on Gaya assimilation that Yushin's own line ('Another man's son may retreat. Mine may not.') already says; cut it. The farmer exchange is a good last beat.

stories.logline: Old Yushin's last visit to the steam cavern, then his deathbed: the king comes, Kangrim asks his question, Munhee asks if he is a Silla man now, Daeto is caught, and after the funeral Wonsul's mother refuses him too.
stories.fixes: The pieces are strong, but the cavern and the deathbed share one 'day' header (block 0); add a scene header at the deathbed. 'Princess…' needs a cue (bridge). The epitaph (25–30) is long and partly repeats Munhee's question; trim to two paragraphs. The Daeto execution (24) lands in the middle of the funeral; move it after the epitaph or into Wanggeom's Guest so the death stays the last big beat before Lady Jiso.

stories.logline: After the funeral Munmu finds his uncle's secret spring, the three goddesses lose their composure over him, pronounce that the west will take his name, and Dangun himself appears on the water to hand him the old title of Wanggeom.
stories.fixes: The visit has a turn (comedy to oracle to Dangun) but no stake: Munmu asks one question and leaves. Give him a want he walks in with (whether to break the oath of Mount Gain, or whether to fight the Tang at sea), so the oracle answers it. Blocks 1 and 5 both say 'the best of both' and repeat 'Gaya shoulders / Surabol mouth' three times; cut the repeats. The end card ('Kim Punghun said he could wait for a ship. The ship is here') is a good bridge into Maeso.

stories.logline: Xue Rengui lands with Punghun as his pilot; a Silla general lets the horses unload and then cuts the beach to pieces, and at Maeso the Silla army steals thirty thousand Mohe horses in a night, with the disgraced Wonsul leading the cut.
stories.fixes: Clear and fun, and it pays off Rebellion and Wonsul. The 'heads?' / 'horses' exchange is a great button. Wonsul's return (block 24) is told in one long paragraph; give him one line or one action on the picket line so the payoff is seen. Punghun is named as pilot and never appears again; either give him a beat on the deck or drop him from the opener. Two closing quotes (34–35) contradict each other on purpose; keep one.

stories.logline: At the mouth of the Geum, a middling captain loses twice to Xue Rengui's fleet, lures it onto the mudflats the third time, and the Tang ships turn west and do not come back.
stories.fixes: Short and clean, but Sideuk is a cipher and Xue never appears in his own last battle. One exchange between Xue and his helmsman as the hulls ground would close his arc (he has been the farmer since Snake River). The formation box and the quote say the same thing; keep one. Ending on Munmu's 'Have we… won…?' works.

stories.logline: Munhee straightens her son's collar on the day he becomes king of all Samhan; five years later he is burned and put under a rock in the sea, and eleven years after that the Tang complain about his father's temple name and drop it at the name of Kim Yushin.
stories.fixes: A good closing chapter for the Silla line, and the mother-and-collar frame is the right first and last image. The two later scene headers are bare years ('681', '692'); rename them to places ('The Sea Tomb / 바다 무덤', 'The Envoy / 당 사신') so they match the other labels and avoid AD years. Block 12 ('Silla lasts nine hundred and ninety-two years') spends a fact the narrator could tease instead.

stories.logline: The winter Pyongyang falls, a Mohe father and his frozen son shelter in a cave; the boy finds a gold branch of the Goguryeo crown in the pack, and the father tells how Yeon Gesomun picked him up from a burned doorway and taught him three words.
stories.fixes: Works on its own and ends the book well; the flashback is properly marked. The map says 720 and the entry is 698 while the scene is the winter of 668; set the entry year to the scene. The coda after 'Cut to black' (31–34) is two summaries and two quotes; keep 'They walk on…' and one quote, and let THE END follow. Block 25's 'By the Holy King's bow' is a nice callback.
